articleTitle: Blockchain-based Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading through a Community-based Virtual Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Developing countries are faced with constant power shortages, which hinders economic growth. The use of fossil fuels has also contributed to this challenge, but now governments have been trying to encourage people to adopt renewable energy at an individual level. This is seen as a long-term solution to the current power challenges. The adoption and use of renewable energy, however, has its own challenges, such as intermittent availability and the high start-up costs. This paper proposes a communitybased virtual power plant (CVPP) with a peer-to-peer energy trading platform as a solution to some of these challenges. CVPPs are decentralized energy systems within a small geographic area that connect small-scale energy producers. The resources of these producers are then pooled together to create a single energy ecosystem. The addition of peer-to-peer energy trading to this setup adds an economic incentive to the members of the CVPP as it allows them to sell excess energy to their neighbours. Blockchain technology acts as a medium of trust in the absence of a trusted third-party. A small-scale prototype for this system was built and tested. Various technologies were used for this prototype such as smart contracts and smart meters.

articleTitle: The Effect of Information Security Awareness, Subjective Norms and Shared Tacit Assumptions on Information Security Culture
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Financial services institutions are one of the prime targets of information security breaches because of the potential of the attackers to reap financial rewards from launching the attacks. Information security culture which is a collection of socio-cultural processes implemented by firms, is forecast to forestall the scourge of information security breaches. Information security culture targets to safeguard the information assets of firms through influencing employees to conduct themselves in a manner that is compatible with the protection of firms’ assets. Information security awareness, subjective norms and shared tacit assumptions are proposed as some of the main determinants of information security culture in the financial services. Therefore, this paper investigates the impact that information security awareness, subjective norms and shared tacit assumptions exert on financial services firms’ information security culture. This paper is a quantitative case study of four financial services firms in Zimbabwe. The results of this study show that information security awareness and subjective norms are predictors of information security culture in the financial services. Conversely, the study established that shared tacit assumptions are not related to information security culture in the financial services.

articleTitle: A Mobile Blockchain-Based Application for Record-Keeping in Branchless Banking Services for Farmers in Qunu
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Blockchain techniques are being used in all industry sectors now as a way of recording and storing information. Although blockchain only started being fully utilized recently, it has shaped many industries, including agriculture. This being the case, many small-scale farmers from the Qunu area in South Africa still do not have bank accounts and therefore cannot provide the credit records required for the funding of their agricultural activities. To counteract this problem, a mobile application called Block Records was developed in this research to help rural farmers have databases of their transaction records and make those records publicly accessible with the use of blockchain technologies. A design science research approach was followed in developing the artefact. This mobile application will enable the farmers to store their records on their mobile devices, print a transaction statement, if necessary, whilst also uploading the information onto a public blockchain platform where the funders can access it. The application developed in this research is a native platform mobile application that is supported only on Android devices.

articleTitle: Financial Services Information Security Culture: The Effect of Technology, People and Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: The digital era has brought about a superfluity of information security attacks most of which are principally aimed at the financial services institutions for commercial gain. The possible safety measure to the plague is the implementation of information security culture. Information security culture targets to safeguard the information assets of organisations by way of influencing humans to conduct themselves in a manner that is compatible with the security of organizational assets. Technology, people and environment are proposed as some of the main determinants of information security culture in the financial services. Therefore, this paper investigates the impact that technology, people and environment exert on financial services firms’ information security culture. This paper is a quantitative case study of four financial services firms in Zimbabwe. The results of this study show that technology and people are both predictors of information security culture in the financial services. However, the results of this study show that the environment does not influence information security culture in the financial services sector. The results of this study enhance the existing knowledge of information security culture through providing empirically grounded evidence of elements that help shape information security culture, a relatively novel domain.

articleTitle: Incident Reporting System: A case for Bulawayo
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Efficient incident reporting stands as a pivotal pillar of urban governance; however, conventional reporting methods frequently fall short in prioritising a comprehensive range of incidents, consequently resulting in suboptimal responses from local authorities. This paper presents the design and implementation of an incident reporting system that enables local residents to report faults within their communities in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe. The build methodology along with Scrum was used to integrate Flutter, Dart, Firebase, and the Google Maps API to create a user-friendly and efficient smart phone based solution. The system was tested using widget test, unit test, functionality test, and system test to ensure that it met all objectives, which include allowing residents to geotag affected areas, generating incident reports, notifying the local authority of new sites and providing geo-fenced warnings for health hazards. The results indicated that residents could use smartphone-based incident reporting system to report faults while local authorities can use the system to respond to reported faults. The system provides logistics and solves problems that result from poor communication and late response to incidents, contributing to better public service delivery in urban areas.

articleTitle: My Baby Growth: Electronic Monitoring of Baby Growth
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: The health sector insists on the accurate keeping of baby growth and immunization records and presenting these on every visit to the doctor or health center. Baby growth and immunization records in some cases are still kept on paper. Paper-based monitoring systems that heavily depend on baby cards pose a challenge to both mothers and caregivers. The card may be lost, smudged, or forgotten at home when trying to seek health assistance. In some cases, mothers forget the date of the next visit, endangering the health of the baby. This paper presents a web-based baby-growth monitoring system that keeps track of selected parameters to monitor baby growth, comparing these with the expected normal, to recommend corrective measures. Our contribution in this paper is an application that eases the process of keeping track of the next baby clinic visits while giving mothers and guardians nutritional advice for healthy baby growth. We build security into the system by modeling both functional and security requirements. This system can be of use to mothers and guardians as it relieves them of the burden of taking care of the card and, at the same time keeping track of the next visit. Medical caregivers can also benefit from the ease provided by the system in gauging baby growth. The health sector can also use the system to derive district and provincial growth averages of children in a country, and thus make necessary policy interventions, based on accurate data.

articleTitle: A Recurrent Neural Networks Model for Early Stroke Detection in Adults
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Stroke is a common illness that results in a wide variety of potentially life-threatening complications. It is the third most prevalent cause of death among people all over the world characterised by the clot or rupture in an artery that stops the flow of blood and nutrients to the brain, which causes the brain to be deprived of oxygen and blood ultimately resulting in death of brain cells. It is important to predict the risk of having a stroke so as to prevent it. The use of predictive approaches in clinical decision-making is becoming increasingly common. These techniques are used to help with issues like the occurrence or diagnosis of disease, the evaluation of prognosis, and assisting physicians in implementing therapies for the disease or its progression. This study implemented supervised machine learning in the diagnosis of stroke at an earlier stage (prediction). The study was informed by the Health Behaviours Theory (HBT), also known as Social Cognitive (SCT). The theory emphasises the individual's own drives to make positive changes in their behaviour. The study adopted the positivist research philosophy, which holds that information gained via measurements is reliable and argues that data should be collected and evaluated objectively in research. The study used secondary data which comprised patients’ diagnosis for stroke. The study used the six-stage Cross Industry Standard Process for Data Mining (CRISP-DM). It was found out that stroke can be predicted using hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, age, family stroke history, BMI and HIV history of the patient and smoking status. After implementing and comparing 9 supervised machine learning algorithms, the study concluded that the Random Forest Classifier correctly predicted stroke with higher metrics of 94.5% and 97.2% K-fold as compared to the other metrics. The algorithm outperformed all others Predicting stroke using the Random Forest Classifier was done with 99% accuracy. The ROC curve of the model indicated a larger area above the diagonal line or below the curve which suggested a higher prediction performance characterised by a low false positive rate. The study contributes significantly to the overall body of knowledge through the application of supervised machine learning algorithms in the prediction of stroke among patients. The application of SMOTE in dealing with imbalanced data sets also introduced a significant contribution to dealing with imbalanced datasets in supervised machine learning. It is important that future studies consider the implementation of convolutional neural networks in which images are used to predict stroke unlike the use of text data as was the case in this study.

articleTitle: Blockchain-based Electronic Voting: Case of Student Council Polls
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: The need for a blockchain-based e-voting system arises from the limitations and vulnerabilities associated with traditional voting methods. While paper-based voting has been the conventional approach for centuries, it is not without its challenges. These challenges include security risks, lack of transparency, limited accessibility and identity verification and privacy concerns. The study shows how blockchain can be implemented in the voting scene and also be able to mitigate the challenges brought about by the paper-based voting system. The methodology employed is linked to software development methodologies. The major findings include the improvement of voting systems in terms of security, transparency and auditability of elections. The use of this research can result in improved election processes.

articleTitle: Author Index
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Taking into consideration that consumers are required and expected to pay their water bills every month. There is a need for a sense of fairness and reasonable billing. Current water billing systems in Zimbabwe overbill users who would not have had their meter readings captured by the meter reader. Also, the idea of having a single meter reader take readings for about two hundred households in a single day raises a cause for concern about the accuracy of the readings due to fatigue. The study designed an application that will enable consumers to upload their meter readings in order to be billed fairly without the use of estimations. This is ethically legal, as the history of the readings will only be visible to the owner of the account and the municipality officials. There is a sense of security guaranteed to the consumer as the users have log in credentials for access to the system. Only one account per meter can be created, so this prevents multiple entries of the same meter in within a household

articleTitle: Leveraging on Cloud IoT as an Evolutionary Step to Contemporary Higher Education. A Case of Zimbabwe's Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Cloud IoT as an emerging technology in the higher education sector, has the ability to connect several devices within and outside campus through a network whilst backed by online storage infrastructure. Consequently, the study sought to investigate the readiness and importance of adopting Cloud IoT for the Zimbabwean higher education institutions to meet the demands of contemporary education. In addition, determining challenges militating against the full implementation of Cloud IoT, as well as providing aimed at harness such technologies. On that note, the study pursued a qualitative research methodology concretized on a constructivist philosophy. Hence, a multiple and exploratory case study targeted 3 universities based in Harare, Zimbabwe. In that regard the study was conducted within 50 participants, pursued through a purposive sampling technique. Most importantly, the study observed that universities are partially ready to adopt Cloud IoT, as they are exposed to challenges ranging from lack of expertise, budgetary constraints and need for comprehensive policy implementation framework.

articleTitle: The Impact of an Online Self-Regulation C-Learn Teaching Tool on Student Performance in Large Computer Programming Class. A Case of Zimbabwean Higher and Tertiary Education.
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: The demand for higher and tertiary education in Africa is now high, and as a result, public institutions are enrolling many students, a phenomenon now called massification [21], [11]. The term massification is defined as the increase in the enrollment of students without a proportionate boost in resources [1], [9]. Zimbabwean universities are enrolling many students to fund operations since government funding has dwindled [5], [8]. The provision of quality education is becoming a challenge due to the high lecturer-student ratio, especially on courses that are highly practical in nature [1]. There is a lack of proper management and engagement of students in very large classes, and as a result, students resort to memorizing content learned instead of engaging in critical thinking [9], [6]. Literature points out that if students develop self-regulated learning strategies, they will overcome challenges brought by massification [14]. The purpose of this study was to develop and evaluate the impact of a multimedia teaching tool in assisting students to develop self-regulated learning strategies so that they improve their performance while learning computer programming in a large class setup. Purposive sampling was used in this study, and the researcher adhered to design science research methodology. Students enrolled in introduction to computer programming used the multimedia CLearn teaching tool that was developed hence purposive sampling was used in this study. One class (BITH131) was the control group and students enrolled in BSIT 131 were the experimental group. Results obtained indicated that students who used the C-Learn teaching tool performed better in a programming test as compared to students in the control group.

articleTitle: A Scalable and Lightweight Authentication Architecture for the Internet of Things (IoT) in Smart Home Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: In the evolving landscape of smart home applications, ensuring robust and efficient authentication within the Internet of Things (IoT) environments is paramount. This paper presents a scalable, lightweight authentication architecture for IoT-driven smart homes. The proposed architecture, drawing inspiration from cloud computing mechanisms, introduces a trusted, smart home agent, integrating the Data-Information-Knowledge-Wisdom (DIKW) model to facilitate efficient and secure data exchange within smart homes. Our solution addresses the challenges of minimal computation and processing overheads, essential in resource-constrained IoT devices, and focuses on device-level authentication to reduce computational costs. A comparative analysis with existing models demonstrates the superiority of our architecture in terms of computational efficiency, making it an ideal candidate for scalable deployments. The architecture successfully navigates the complexities of ensuring secure communication among autonomous IoT devices, balancing the dual needs of computational efficiency and robust security, thereby promising resilience against common security threats in the smart home ecosystem.

articleTitle: Copyright Page
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: In this modern age, Automatic Number Plate Recognition systems are an important aspect to improve service efficiency (toll collection, traffic management, parking management), security (vehicle tracking, monitoring vehicle visits) and law enforcement when dealing with motor vehicles. However, many of the existing Automatic Number Plate Recognition systems were developed for countries with number plate standards and font that differ from the Zimbabwean number plates. This research compares different approaches to Automatic Number Plate Recognition techniques with a special focus on Zimbabwean number plates through experiments. The experiments were grouped into two main phases of Automatic Number Plate Recognition namely plate detection and plate recognition. The experiments for plate detection compared traditional image processing techniques using OpenCV and deep learning techniques using the YOLOv8 algorithm. The YOLOv8 algorithm proved to be the most accurate approach for plate detection. Experiments for plate recognition compared Optical Character Recognition engines and machine learning approaches. The compared machine learning algorithms were random forest classifier, and K-Nearest Neighbour. In this set of experiments, a K-Nearest Neighbour algorithm proved to be quicker and more accurate in detecting Zimbabwean number plates. This research recommends the development of an end-to-end system for Zimbabwean number plates recognition using deep learning.

articleTitle: Automated Ticket Classification for Information Technology Helpdesks using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Manual ticket classification is a time-consuming and error-prone process that often leads to misclassification and increases the time it takes to resolve issues. This research investigates using machine learning to classify IT helpdesk tickets automatically. This research uses the GridSearchCV, RandomizedSearchCV, and KFold validation for parameter tuning on three algorithms, KNN, SVM, and Random Forest classifiers, to improve the accuracy of the ticket classifier system. The performance of the classifiers with hyper-tuned parameters was checked against the individual base classifiers using the accuracy score performance metric. KNN and SVM classifiers with hyper-tuned parameters performed better than the corresponding base classifiers. On the contrary, hyperparameter tuning on the Random Forest classifier decreased its prediction accuracy. Overall, the SVM classifier with tuned parameters was the best, with an accuracy score of 94.6%. The dataset was unbalanced, so under-sampling was performed to balance the classes. The results of this study show that machine learning effectively automates ticket classification for IT helpdesks. This can lead to faster resolution times, increased customer satisfaction, and business growth. The study also provides recommendations for future research in evaluating different dataset-balancing approaches.

articleTitle: Financial Services Information Security Culture Strategies
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: The digital era has been accompanied by an overabundance of information security attacks the bulk of which are predominantly directed at the financial services firms for financial gain. The possible safety measure to the menace of information security breaches is the refinement of information security culture. Information security culture strives to guard the information assets of firms by the way of influencing humans to conduct themselves in a way that is compatible with the safeguarding of organizational assets. Temporal strategies, spatial strategies, information security awareness and information security education and training are proposed as some of the main determinants of information security culture in the financial services. Therefore, this paper investigates the impact that temporal strategies, spatial strategies, information security awareness and information security education and training exert on financial services firms’ information security culture. This paper is a quantitative case study of four financial services firms in Zimbabwe. The results of this study show that temporal strategies, spatial strategies and information security awareness are not related to information security culture in the financial services. On the other hand, information security education and training is a predictor of information security culture in the financial services.

articleTitle: Sustainable ICT Hubs for Rural Schooling in Developing Countries. The Case of Makoni District, Zimbabwe
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: This study was motivated by the need for economically and environmentally sustainable ICT hubs in marginalized rural schools in pursuit of sustainable development goals (SDGs). Affordability and availability of ICT infrastructure and resources are the prime factors in the digital divide. Hence, there is need for a cost-effective means to be strategically implemented for the purpose of achieving educational objectives in this information society. Therefore, the study adopted a qualitative research design which employed interviews, questionnaires and observations. A single case study design was pursued for 25 rural primary and secondary schools in Makoni District, Manicaland province of Zimbabwe which comprised of 50 participants. In that respect, findings from the study unearthed that quite a number of schools do not have sufficient ICT infrastructure to enjoy the benefits of ICT centred education. Worse still, some of the schools are not connected to the electricity grid which makes them not ready to pursue ICT based education. Consequently, the study proposed an ICT Hub strategy to serve schools and surrounding communities with the latest digital technologies, thus creating an information rich society and further contributes to global economic transformation

articleTitle: Tomato Leaf Disease Detection System Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: The tomato leaf disease detection system using convolutional neural networks (CNN) is a computer visionbased approach to automate the identification of tomato leaf disease. Convolutional neural network is an artificial neural network, which is used widely in prediction. The system is a web-based application that allows farmers to upload images then get real-time results on whether the leaf uploaded is healthy or not. The system also prescribes detected disease treatment options. In Zimbabwe, leaf diseases in tomatoes are increasingly becoming common. The diseases affect the quality and quantity of tomato fruit output leading to poor yields and low monetary return on Agri-investments. Tomato leaf diseases are common problems in the farming industry, mostly in Zimbabwe as the field has become one of most paying fields, these problems affect the quality and quantity of tomato plants. The research aimed to develop a classifier that in real time predicts disease results from a tomato leaf image upload. The dataset of tomato leaves was downloaded from Kaggle, the dataset was used to train the classification model as well as testing the model for prediction accuracy. The study involved the collection of the dataset of tomato leaf images, pre-processing the images, training the CNN model and developing the web application. The accuracy of the system's performance was 93% which is a good result in that the farmers can rely on the system's classification.

articleTitle: Title Page
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: This study aims to understand how students perceive the usage of Learning Management Systems (LMSs). A descriptive survey design was used. A sample of 50 students was randomly selected from the information systems department. For data triangulation, 10 lecturers were purposively selected for the study. For data collection semi-structured questionnaire, focus group discussions, and online survey were engaged. Descriptive statistics were used to analyse quantitative data while qualitative data was manually analyzed according to emerging themes. Research findings show that implementation of LMS is at times punctuated with challenges such as poor internet connectivity, exorbitant data, lack of knowledge and skills as well as insufficient student orientation. Furthermore, students showed that they were satisfied with the implementation of LMS and acknowledged through improved pass rate. The study recommended that training, workshops, and investing in more inappropriate mobile devices are integral components in improving LMS implementation.

articleTitle: Table of Contents
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the leading causes of cancer-related death worldwide. Early detection and diagnosis of CRC is critical for successful treatment and improved patient outcomes. The development of deep learning models for CRC prediction has the potential to revolutionize the way that CRC is identified and managed. The purpose of the study is to create a CRC prediction model that can be used in clinical settings to accurately identify colorectal cancer as early as possible. The experiments were conducted using the Fastai library, which provides a high-level interface for deep learning tasks. A pre-trained ResNet-34 model architecture was utilized, which has been proven effective for various image classification tasks. To optimize the model’s performance, hyperparameter tuning experiments were conducted. Through the utilization of CNNs and other deep learning architectures, it has been demonstrated that histopathological images can be accurately analyzed to detect colorectal cancer. The evaluation metrics, including accuracy (95.6%), confusion matrix, and ROC curve, demonstrate the model’s ability to accurately classify colorectal tissue samples. The findings align with existing literature on colorectal cancer prediction, validating the effectiveness of our proposed model. The study recommends that larger and more diverse datasets must be used to improve the accuracy and reliability of detection systems, larger since they will represent different populations and subtypes of cancer are needed.

articleTitle: Developing a Predictive Machine Learning Model to Determine the Likelihood of Readmission of Substance Abuse Patients in Zimbabwe
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: This research aimed to address the issue of readmissions of substance use patients in Zimbabwe. The data used was obtained from one of the biggest psychiatric hospitals in Zimbabwe that offers outpatients and early rehabilitation services to psychotic patients. The dataset consisted of 1246 rows, 30 columns, and 921 unique patients. The features were combined to develop a predictive model that had a very good performance because it considered a cocktail of variables. The model accuracy, precision, recall, F1 Score and AUC-ROC had scores above 97%. The Model Prototype was successfully deployed via a web-based platform to determine the likelihood of readmission of substance abuse patients on a scale of 0% to 100%. The major findings from the research are: 1) readmission is not one factor determined but is a factor of different influencers combined, 2) the most commonly used substances inducing psychosis in Zimbabwe were found to be alcohol, crystal meth, marijuana and nicotine, 3) substance-induced psychosis is exponentially increasing and geographically spanned because admitted patients came from 51 different towns, cities or town councils all over Zimbabwe. These findings provided actionable insights and recommendations for the ministry, which declared a national concern of substance abuse and henceforth launched a five-year ‘Zimbabwe National Drug Master Plan’ (ZNDMP 2020-2025). This study provides the target age group to focus interventions on.

articleTitle: An Integrated Web based Patient Records Application for Sustainable Healthcare Services
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: The role of big data analytics in health care, particularly within the Eastern Cape Health Care System, is a burgeoning field with immense potential. The ability to leverage vast amounts of data to inform decision making, optimize resource allocation, and improve patient outcomes is a transformative shift in healthcare delivery and management. This study presents an integrated web-based system that incorporates predictive analytics, real-time monitoring functionality, patient record management and clinical decision support capabilities, thus resulting in improved patient centred care and enhanced resource allocation. MasiphileHIS is a webbased system that has been developed mainly for the Eastern Cape Public Clinics. The implementation of the all-inclusive records system will afford more standardised and streamlined processes in rural based health institutions. The study employed a quantitative approach through utilization of secondary data to formulate requirements for the Health Information System (HIS). A series of workshops were conducted which resulted in the development of the locally produced system for the people of the Eastern Cape Province. This proposed solution assists people in rural areas in the Eastern Cape province to have easier access to healthcare services and information.

articleTitle: Fostering a Cyber Security Culture & Cyber Hygiene Among the Generation Z. A Synthesis Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Online users who act irresponsibly or improperly raise the risk of a security attack on the information systems they use. Despite the fact that device technical security is always getting better, recent studies have shown that the human element continues to pose a serious threat to the system. A strong cyber security culture and good cyber hygiene can lessen this threat. The purpose of this paper is to highlight the importance of fostering a cyber security culture & cyber hygiene among the generation Z. This study used a synthesis approach when conducting literature review. The literature also identified gaps in young people's cyber hygiene, cyber security culture, and awareness, as well as possible future directions for some of the issues.

articleTitle: A Mobile WebRTC-Based Platform to Support Young and Upcoming Researchers
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Lack of research support is impacting the research capacity in Zimbabwean universities, which calls for a system that supports young and upcoming researchers to be put in place. The problems that arise as a result of the status quo are that research output is lagging behind that of other countries, developing research capacity is impacted, quality research is lacking, and the critical research skills gap which hampers economic recovery is widening. The intention of this research is to develop a mobile WebRTC-based platform to connect established researchers with young and upcoming researchers for guidance and support and to enable peer-to-peer learning. This therefore is a form of knowledge management platform that encourages knowledge dissemination among Zimbabwean academics. This research builds a mobile application that allows young researchers to collaborate with more experienced researchers and peers. While the experienced researchers will use this technology to guide the young researchers, the platform will also encourage peer-to-peer learning. The application consists of the three APIs of the WebRTC platform of peer-to-peer learning, multipoint conferencing, and selective forwarding to build a rich environment for interaction between the researchers.

articleTitle: A framework for the adoption of blockchain technology in boosting value added tax collection by the Zimbabwe Revenue Authority
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Since the invention of the internet, technology continued to evolve around it bringing about innovations that improved processes to become more efficient and effective. Businesses around the world have adopted technology changes while tax administrators lagged. ZIMRA first automated VAT in 2010 through the adoption of Fiscal Electronic Tax Registers that recorded sales at retail shops and generated fiscal receipts. The objective of this research was to develop a framework for ZIMRA to adopt blockchain technology to further enhance the automation of VAT collection. A literature review and a conceptual framework were used to conduct focus group meetings. Thematic data analysis based on Braun and Clarke, six phases. Four themes were identified which are; the role of stakeholders, technology advancement and resources, corruption and complex legislation, telecommunications and infrastructure. Finally, these themes were synthesized into a framework which reviewed by three experts. A framework was then proposed. Thus, is possible to resolve non-compliance issues that included a lack of transparency and corrupt tendencies through the blockchain platform, whereby VAT would be remitted in realtime. The benefits to ZIMRA would be total control of the VAT process, eliminating intermediaries, and encouraging voluntary compliance. Therefore, this study can assist researchers in the continent to develop new knowledge on how Africa, especially the public sector, can use the technology to add value to their countries.

articleTitle: A Systematic Review of Customised Career Recommender Systems for South Africa
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: The rise of computers and ICTs decades ago has gradually changed the life of all individuals across the world. With the Internet and technology in career counselling services and resources, both counsellors and clients are positively and negatively affected. With the growing interest in the personalization of services, career recommendations have seen an exponential growth with the technology savvy graduates and unemployed youth. This systematic review therefore focuses on the important role that personalised career recommendation systems play, as well as the various factors that can are used in developing personalized career recommendations in South Africa. This study will assist by providing effective career guidance and personalized recommendations to individuals in different contexts and settings. Google Scholar, IEEE Digital Library, Web of Science and ACM Digital Library were used to search for research publications for a period of ten years, from 2010 to 2020, which focused on personalized career recommendation systems. After the vetting process, a total of 25 articles were selected and presented in this systematic review. The findings of this study show the benefits of using personalised career recommendation systems outweigh the concerns and drawbacks that comes with artificial intelligence founded solutions. Suggestions from this review is to investigate further the link between various digital technologies that can be considered especially in the sphere of the computer's cognitive intelligence.

articleTitle: Colorectal Cancer Prediction using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the leading causes of cancer-related death worldwide. Early detection and diagnosis of CRC is critical for successful treatment and improved patient outcomes. The development of deep learning models for CRC prediction has the potential to revolutionize the way that CRC is identified and managed. The purpose of the study is to create a CRC prediction model that can be used in clinical settings to accurately identify colorectal cancer as early as possible. The experiments were conducted using the Fastai library, which provides a high-level interface for deep learning tasks. A pre-trained ResNet-34 model architecture was utilized, which has been proven effective for various image classification tasks. To optimize the model's performance, hyperparameter tuning experiments were conducted. Through the utilization of CNNs and other deep learning architectures, it has been demonstrated that histopathological images can be accurately analyzed to detect colorectal cancer. The evaluation metrics, including accuracy (95.6%), confusion matrix, and ROC curve, demonstrate the model's ability to accurately classify colorectal tissue samples. The findings align with existing literature on colorectal cancer prediction, validating the effectiveness of our proposed model. The study recommends that larger and more diverse datasets must be used to improve the accuracy and reliability of detection systems, larger since they will represent different populations and subtypes of cancer are needed. (Abstract)

articleTitle: The Role of Higher Education Institutions in Promoting Industrialisation in Zimbabwe
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: The role of universities in promoting industrialisation in Zimbabwe has attracted much interest among academia and researchers nationwide. These Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) constitute several governments' grand strategies for promoting the development of small-scale industries. The purpose of this paper is to examine the role of Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) in promoting industrialisation in Zimbabwe. The study adopted the pragmatism research which integrates both the positivism and interpretivism research paradigms. The study followed the mixed methods approach in which both quantitative and qualitative data collection was conducted through in-depth online interviews and questionnaires due to COVID-19 restrictions. The descriptive research design was employed as it is best suited in mixed-method research. Respondents were drawn from industry and state universities through convenience and purposive sampling. Quantitative data was edited and coded for quantitative analyses using the Statistical Package for Social Scientists (SPSS) whilst the qualitative data from the interview and document reviews was analysed using content and thematic analysis. On data testing, inferential statistics was adopted and used. The results of the study revealed that the role of HEIs in promoting industrialisation is underpinned by factors such as organisational structure, culture, availability, and adequacy of infrastructure. Furthermore, HEIs also provide skilled manpower for industry through the creation of entrepreneurial spirit and culture among students. The study recommends that sector-specific training programmes must be provided for the manufacturing, retail, and services sectors. Additionally, the curriculum needs to be reviewed such that it is in line with industry expectations as well as the Doctrine Education 5.0. Innovation hubs and industrial parks established at universities must encourage industry-based outcomes and solutions that will spur industrialisation. HEIs should partner with the government and the industry to effectively support the development of industrialisation in Zimbabwe.

articleTitle: Investigating the Effects of Digital Pornography on University Students in Zimbabwe and Proposing an Empowering 8-way Pornography Reduction Model
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd Zimbabwe Conference of Information and Communication Technologies (ZCICT)
abstract: This research examines the effects of digital pornography on university students in Zimbabwe, focusing on the ignorance of relevant information and its connection to undesirable behavior. Concerned about the high rates of Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) resulting from this ignorance, the study collected quantitative data from a sample of 1500 university students (64% male, 36% female) from Chinhoyi University of Technology (CUT). The review encompassed demographic information, porn use and perception, the Compulsive Internet Use Scale (mCIUS) to measure habitual web porn use, and questions on emotional and sexual states related to porn use (EmSS). Findings indicate that porn use negatively impacts social relationships (58.7%), mental health (63.9%), sexual performance (67.7%), and psychosocial development in youth and adolescence (78.1%). The research highlights a significant correlation between literacy ignorance, porn use, and behavior addiction leading to increased STIs. Recommendations include awareness campaigns, on-campus/off-campus talk shows, sensitization workshops, and the introduction of technology with a machine learning-based Short Message Service (SMS) engine to generate warnings against pornography which lead to the creation of an 8-way pornography reduction model.
